where: Worked example 1 (also Section 1 formula notes and Quiz Q5)
problem: The symbol σy is used for two different quantities in the same sentence: the normal stress in the y direction (σy = −40 MPa) and the tensile yield strength (σy = 250 MPa). The formula notes also define 'σy is the tensile yield strength' while σx, σy are defined as normal stresses. A student cannot tell which σy the numbers belong to, and the factor of safety 250/152.32 is meaningless if σy is read as the −40 MPa stress.
fix: Use one symbol for yield strength and keep σx, σy for the stress components. For example: 'σx = 100 MPa, σy = −40 MPa, τxy = 30 MPa and yield strength σY = 250 MPa'. In the formula notes write 'σY is the tensile yield strength in MPa' and write the criteria as σeq,T ≤ σY and σeq,M ≤ σY. Do the same in Quiz Q5 (σx = 80 MPa, σy = 20 MPa, τxy = 40 MPa, σY = 220 MPa) and in Quiz Q7 (σY = 300 MPa).

problem: It says the von Mises stress is the root-mean-square of the three principal differences. It is not. The RMS of the differences (σ1−σ2), (σ2−σ3), (σ3−σ1) is √{[(σ1−σ2)²+(σ2−σ3)²+(σ3−σ1)²]/3}, while σeq,M is √{[(σ1−σ2)²+(σ2−σ3)²+(σ3−σ1)²]/2}. The von Mises value is √(3/2) ≈ 1.225 times that RMS, not equal to it. In the worked example the RMS of 152.32, 46.16 and 106.16 MPa is 110.5 MPa, but σeq,M is 135.3 MPa.
fix: Write: 'The von Mises value is √(3/2) times the root-mean-square of the three principal differences, so it still cannot exceed the largest difference.'

where: Section 2, last sentence of the octahedral paragraph
problem: 'the mean stress (σ1+σ2+σ3)/3 only moves the plane along its normal' is unclear and misleading. The mean stress is the normal stress acting on the octahedral plane; it does not move the plane and does not change the octahedral shear.
fix: Write: 'the mean stress (σ1+σ2+σ3)/3 is the normal stress on the octahedral plane; it changes volume only and leaves τoct unchanged.'

problem: 'Stress offices use these' is unexplained jargon. A reader meeting the phrase for the first time will not know it means the stress-analysis group in a design organisation.
fix: Write: 'Stress engineers in design offices use these to turn a multiaxial state into one equivalent stress that is compared with the yield strength σY.'

problem: 'The von Mises factor 1.25 is acceptable only when the code is validated for the material' is ambiguous and loosely argued. 'Code' can be read as finite element software or as a design code, and 'validated for the material' is not the usual reason. The standard practice is: von Mises is the normal criterion for ductile metals; a Tresca check is added when a conservative lower bound is wanted.
fix: Answer: 'Report the lower (Tresca) factor, 300/260 = 1.15, as the conservative check. The von Mises factor 300/240 = 1.25 is the usual value for design of ductile metals, but it is not conservative because Tresca always bounds von Mises from above.'
